articles.title: Inside Google’s AI training for teachers
articles.summary: Google flew 70 teachers and administrators to its California headquarters to learn about its AI products — and how to persuade skeptical colleagues to use them.
articles.body: MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. — Sitting in an atrium on Google’s campus, a group of K-12 educators imagined the worst response they could receive when they tried to persuade their colleagues to use artificial intelligence. They pictured a veteran English teacher who was still upset that cursive is no longer taught. Perhaps she would yell that AI is “just another shiny tech fad.” What’s next, she might ask — robots teaching kids how to read? The educators asked Gemini, Google’s AI assistant, for advice and soon had a role-playing plan. They would win over this skeptical English teacher by explaining what generative AI could do for her: create classroom materials for phonics lessons, reducing what would normally be hours of work to just two minutes. The key, the educators agreed, was to avoid getting into an argument or letting this AI critic unload all her fears uninterrupted. “Well, it’s not cursive, but it did save me an hour of typing tonight,” they predicted the English teacher would eventually reply. Seventy teachers and school technology directors selected for their interest in Google’s education technology products traveled to the company’s headquarters last week for a free two-day training program on how to use AI — and how to urge their colleagues to use it, too. The Google Educator Series is part of the company’s long-standing effort to put its products in schools, and this training signaled the company’s growing focus on AI. Most of the attendees said their colleagues back home were “cautiously curious” about AI. In the breakout session that included the role-playing exercise, the training’s leaders suggested responding to resistance by focusing on “pain points” and how Google’s tools, including Gemini and NotebookLM, an AI research assistant, could solve them. “It’s not as scary if you’ve taken something off of my plate versus giving me a new thing that I have to then go out and learn,” Winston Roberts, director of an AI initiative at ISTE+ASCD, a nonprofit education group that worked with Google to develop the training, told educators from a stage. The guidance on overcoming pushback reflects the increasingly hostile public sentiment toward AI as an expanding grassroots movement of parents demands less reliance on computers in schools. In the month before the training, Pope Leo XIV urged more regulations to slow AI adoption, college graduates booed ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt and other commencement speakers when they promoted AI, and one of the country’s largest teachers unions called for limits on AI and screen time in elementary schools. AI is playing a larger role in classrooms: Some states already require schools to provide AI instruction, universities are paying millions to provide chatbots for students, and the federal government is prioritizing AI in education grants. But recent surveys found most teachers have not received guidance on how to use AI in their work. Jennie Magiera, global head of education impact at Google, said in an interview during the training that teachers and students are going to continue using AI more as it advances. She said Google wants to train as many teachers as possible so they can “harness the power” of AI and “use it for good.” Some teachers at the training said they were glad to have the chance to learn about the rapidly evolving technology rather than being left to figure it out themselves. Karen Compton, an English teacher at a middle school in Ewa Beach, Hawaii, said that AI rarely came up in her classroom last year but that it’s “all over the place” now and she had to figure it out quickly. AI is a part of students’ vocabulary — they refer to things they think aren’t real as AI — and she feels a responsibility to make sure they know what they’re talking about. “If a student’s running in the hallway, you don’t take away the hallway — you teach them the proper behavior for the hallway,” Compton said. “And I think this mimics that in the same way.” In May, Google rolled out free online training modules on its AI tools for K-12 administrators and educators, and college faculty members, with guidance about creating study guides, crafting lesson plans and analyzing where students are getting stuck. The training materials describe Gemini as “an engine for high-quality instruction” to do the “heavy lifting” for designing classroom lessons. “As an educator, this shift moves you into the role of a ‘learning conductor,’” one slide states. Google plans to release additional modules monthly starting in September to capture developments in the technology. “It’s really, really important that we use it,” Joseph South, chief innovation officer for ISTE+ASCD, the nonprofit group working with Google, said of AI at last week’s training. “We can’t just ignore it, we can’t ban it, we can’t keep it out of our schools — that’s not gonna prepare us for the future.” Google has offered training in its products for teachers for two decades, before it began promoting its Chromebook operating system as a way for school districts to provide a laptop for every student. Chromebooks now dominate the education technology market. In an undated presentation, Google described its presence in schools as a way to build a “pipeline of future users,” according to internal company documents revealed in court that NBC News first reported on in January. Additional internal records, unsealed in court filings in February, indicate that Google has long considered how AI could be used in schools. A 2018 presentation about keeping Google at the top of the education technology space said schools wanted more “Personalized Learning” and “Adaptive Content” and identified machine learning and AI as major trends it could seize upon. “Educators are sitting on a growing goldmine of data,” the presentation said, but they needed help organizing and making sense of it. If Google designed ways for schools to use student data, it would set “the stage for us to reinvent the education system through data.” A Google spokesperson previously said that the heavily redacted internal documents released through court filings “mischaracterize our work” and that the company has responded to schools’ demand for its products. Magiera, a former Chicago public school teacher, said her goal in the recent training is to show educators how Google’s products can transform their jobs. “What we’re bringing AI here to do is to help create new pathways to overcome the obstacles that you’ve been facing and to create ways to reach new goals that you never dreamed possible with your learners,” she said. “It’s not going to be easy; I’m not trying to be naive about it. The probability that educators will be able to make that opportunity a reality is greatly increased when we give them training and support.” Speakers at the training emphasized that humans should always stay involved with any AI use and that technology shouldn’t replace teachers. They focused instead on how a teacher could use Gemini to create a comic strip that explains how greenhouse gases trap heat, for example, or how elementary school children could use AI to generate more realistic depictions of their ideas than they are capable of drawing. Casey Cuny, a high school English teacher in a Los Angeles suburb, described asking his students to debate their takeaways from readings — like the concept of “doublethink” from “1984” by George Orwell — with Gemini before discussing them in class. “It’s the best discourse I’ve seen in years on some of these Socratic seminars I’ve been running in my classes,” he said. “It does push the thinking when used intentionally and strategically. And remember that I’m still using teaching methods — I’m not just putting it on the AI and walking away.” As the educators left the Googleplex to return to their school districts, they knew they would face challenges in evangelizing for AI. Parents in many states are forming groups to protest AI in schools, and in some places, they’re winning. But Mike Amante, a technology teacher in New Hartford, New York, said the training equipped him to show skeptics how AI could be beneficial to learning — not just for cheating. “They may not like it, but I don’t think that’s going to change things,” he said. “The naysayers are not going to stop it.”

articles.title: Sammy 'The Bull' Gravano recalls chilling mob request that helped clear John Gotti's path to power
articles.summary: Sammy Gravano reveals the shocking moment Angelo Ruggiero asked him to help John Gotti kill Gambino crime family boss Paul Castellano.
articles.body: Former Gambino crime family underboss Sammy "The Bull" Gravano dished on the moment he was asked to help pull off one of the mob's most audacious power plays — the murder of John Gotti's own boss. "We have problems with Paul. I need your help. We need you — me and John Gotti," Gravano recalled being told by Gotti associate Angelo Ruggiero. "I said, 'To do what?'" he recounted on the "Hang Out With Sean Hannity" podcast. SAMMY 'THE BULL' REVEALS WHY HIS LOVE FOR JOHN GOTTI TURNED INTO PRISON HATE "We're gonna kill him." The target was Paul Castellano, then-boss of the Gambino crime family, one of the most powerful figures in organized crime — making the request anything but an ordinary mob "favor." "You're gonna kill the boss of bosses?" Gravano recalled asking, prompting Ruggiero to respond, "Yes, and we need your help." The gravity of the request wasn't lost on him, he told host Sean Hannity. A hit on a boss could carry serious — even deadly — consequences for everyone involved. Gravano recalled pressing the issue and asking where Gotti was himself. JOHN GOTTI PAL: I STASHED $10M IN MY KID'S TOYCHEST "I told him, 'Angelo, first of all, where's John Gotti? You're talking to me. Where is he?'" The back-and-forth between the two men continued, with Ruggiero insisting that Gotti "had something to do." "[I said], 'He had something more important than asking me to kill the boss of bosses or help you kill the boss of bosses? I don't know what's more important than that,'" Gravano recounted. "This is a big deal," he added. Castellano and his new underboss, Thomas Bilotti, were ultimately murdered outside a New York City steakhouse in 1985. Gotti was the mastermind behind the incident and would soon be convicted for ordering the crime. Gravano's sit-down conversation with Hannity went beyond the incident, into his time with the mob, his involvement in nearly 20 murders and much more. articles.title: Emirates convierte piezas de aviones retirados en el nuevo escudo del Arsenal
articles.standfirst: La compañía aérea ha reutilizado componentes de aeronaves, para crear una versión del escudo del club londinense como parte de su programa de reciclaje
articles.summary: La compañía aérea ha reutilizado componentes de aeronaves, para crear una versión del escudo del club londinense como parte de su programa de reciclaje
articles.body: Lo que a primera vista parece una enorme pieza decorativa del Arsenal tiene, en realidad, una historia mucho más curiosa detrás. Emirates ha conseguido transformar diferentes componentes de aviones retirados en una réplica del icónico escudo del club inglés, dando una segunda vida a materiales que ya no podían volver a utilizarse en aeronaves. El proyecto ha sido desarrollado por el equipo de ingeniería de Emirates Aircraft Engineering, que se encarga de desmontar y reciclar diferentes piezas durante los trabajos de mantenimiento de los aviones. En esta ocasión, el resultado ha sido especialmente llamativo: un escudo construido prácticamente desde cero con elementos procedentes de aeronaves. Para construir la pieza se utilizaron componentes muy diferentes. Algunas partes de la cara del escudo proceden de elementos estructurales retirados, mientras que el característico cañón del Arsenal fue elaborado a partir de una estructura de conductos. Uno de los elementos más curiosos es la rueda, que perteneció directamente a un Airbus A380. Pero hay más. Los ingenieros aprovecharon también piezas de asientos, paneles del suelo y componentes de las bodegas de carga para crear los pequeños detalles del escudo. Incluso las letras fueron fabricadas utilizando partes procedentes de paneles de la cabina y de las ventanas de los aviones. Una vez terminada la estructura, el proyecto pasó por las manos del mismo equipo encargado de pintar los aviones de Emirates. El acabado final permitió darle al escudo una apariencia completamente nueva sin perder el origen de los materiales utilizados. Después de todo el proceso de fabricación, la pieza viajó hasta Londres y encontró su nuevo hogar en el Emirates Stadium, reforzando los 20 años de colaboración entre la aerolínea y el Arsenal.El proyecto es un ejemplo de cómo materiales que podrían haber terminado simplemente desechados pueden convertirse en algo completamente diferente. Nada se pierde, las piezas de un avión retirado pueden volver a la vida, esta vez convertidas en un símbolo del fútbol.

articles.title: Las encuestas confirman la 'caída de los influencers': el dato que revela la bajada de seguidores en estos perfiles
articles.standfirst: Siguen contando con muchos seguidores, pero aumenta la percepción del contenido publicitario
articles.summary: Siguen contando con muchos seguidores, pero aumenta la percepción del contenido publicitario
articles.body: Los influencers están atravesando un momento complicado. Los creadores de contenido en redes sociales, principalmente en Instagram y TikTok, están sufriendo una bajada de seguidores que, a pesar de ser irrelevante comparada a los seguidores que tienen, ha abierto el debate sobre la caída de los influencers. El descenso de la figura de los divulgadores se debe principalmente a dos razones: la cada vez mayor percepción de la publicidad encubierta y las polémicas de ciertos creadores que opinan de temas en los que no son expertos. Uno de los que ha sufrido críticas por una de estas últimas polémicas es Carlos García, Carliyoelnervio en redes, que afirmó que el eclipse solar del pasado 12 de agosto es “una cortina de humo” para que no se hable de otros problemas de la sociedad. Las reacciones por parte de otros creadores sobre los que opinan de temas que no conocen no han tardado en llegar. Es el caso del youtuber y streamer DjMariio, quién en un extracto de un vídeo en directo dió su opinión acerca de la caída de los influencers. “Es normal que os funen”, comenzaba el youtuber. “Vivimos superbien, de algo que nos gusta, nos divertimos… ¡Callaté, callaté!”, concluyó. Por otro lado, los seguidores comienzan a desarrollar una mayor percepción del contenido publicitario encubierto. La vigésimo octava edición de la encuesta ‘Navegantes en la Red’, elaborada por la Asociación para la Investigación de Medios de Comunicación (AIMC), ha revelado que el 69,8% de la audiencia cree que los influencers abusan de la publicidad encubierta. Por otro lado, hay influencers que pierden seguidores por actos o comportamientos polémicos. Es el caso de la influencer RoRo, quién ha sufrido una bajada de medio millón de seguidores durante los días después a su participación en ‘La Velada del año 6’. RoRo protagonizó una de las mayores polémicas del evento al imponer pelear con un casco que prácticamente le tapa toda la cara. Su argumento fue que era el único casco que le permitía pelear debido a una operación de nariz. Natalia Palacios, Fabiana Sevillano o Javi Hoyos son otros de los creadores de contenido que están perdiendo seguidores debido a diferentes polémicas.

articles.title: Florida woman accused of hiding thousands in stolen cash inside body after allegedly scamming senior
articles.summary: Moniquie Love Turnbull allegedly posed as a bank representative to scam a senior citizen then entered jail with $3,200 in cash hidden in her body.
articles.body: A Florida woman accused of posing as a bank representative to scam a senior citizen allegedly carried the scheme all the way to jail, where authorities said they found $3,200 in cash hidden inside her body. Moniquie Love Turnbull, 31, of Miami, was arrested after Martin County Sheriff's Office (MCSO) deputies alleged she showed up at a senior citizen's home pretending to work for the alleged victim's bank. The MCSO said Turnbull told the victim the account had been compromised and tried to obtain the person's debit or credit card under the guise of disposing of it. NEW BANK SCAM LAWS COULD STOP SUSPICIOUS PAYMENTS The alleged victim became suspicious and contacted law enforcement. While deputies investigated, they received another call identifying Turnbull as a possible suspect in a similar case, according to the MCSO. Deputies located Turnbull driving near Interstate 95 before she could leave Martin County and arrested her on fraud charges Monday during a traffic stop caught on MCSO bodycam video. Turnbull faces charges of scheme to defraud, felony use of a two-way communication device and fraudulent use of a credit or debit card without consent involving a victim 60 or older, according to the MCSO. TWO MEN ACCUSED OF POSING AS FEDERAL AGENTS ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TARGETING 85-YEAR-OLD IN $200K GOLD SCAM The case took another turn after Turnbull was brought to jail. Authorities said Turnbull entered the prison with $3,200 in cash lodged in her vagina. "It’s not clear who the money was taken from, but for now, it’s accounted for and sealed in evidence," the MCSO said in a social media post. "Keep in mind, at some point the cash will be back in public circulation." FLORIDA WOMAN TELLS POLICE SHE KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT DRUGS THAT ALLEGEDLY FELL OUT OF HER ‘JAIL PURSE’ Turnbull faces an additional charge of introduction of contraband into a prison. Her bond was set at $500,000, the sheriff's office said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After the arrest, the MCSO warned people not to hand over credit cards, cash, gold or other valuables to anyone who unexpectedly shows up at a home claiming to represent a bank, financial institution, government agency or other organization. Authorities advised anyone confronted with a similar situation not to allow the person inside or give them valuables and instead call 911.

articles.title: Un león en Toledo: drones y un helicóptero para encontrarlo
articles.standfirst: Un repartidor avista supuestamente al felino y las autoridades examinan la zona
articles.summary: Un repartidor avista supuestamente al felino y las autoridades examinan la zona
articles.body: Hay un león suelto en Toledo. Supuestamente. Un repartido afirma haber avistado a este imponente felino cerca del convento del Piélago, en la Sierra de San Vicente, y las autoridades no han encontrado indicios de su presencia. De todas formas, la Guardia Civil se ha puesto manos a la obra y está usando, desde la mañana de este 20 de agosto, drones y un helicóptero, procedente de la Comunidad de Madrid, para salir de dudas. Las autoridades han preguntado a los zoológicos de la zona para confirmar si algún león, o un animal similar, se había escapado en las últimas horas. El Zoo Safari Fauna Aventura, de Toledo, ha asegurado en un comunicado que no falta ningún animal: "Rogamos que no se difundan acusaciones falsas vinculando este avistamiento con nuestro zoo". Por su parte, los ayuntamientos cercanos han advertido a sus ciudadanos que sean prudentes y que eviten caminos secundarios. Esteban Sánchez, teniente de alcalde de Hinojosa de San Vicente, ha valorado la situación en declaraciones a 'Mañaneros'. "No sabemos de dónde puede salir. Las autoridades se han puesto en contacto con todos los safaris de la zona y de ningún safari falta ningún animal. No podemos saber de dónde pueden venir. El pueblo está tranquilo, está tomando las precauciones que se le ha dicho que tome", ha afirmado con tono calmado. Algunas informaciones apuntan a la posibilidad de que en realidad el animal avistado por el repartidor, concretamente en el kilómetro nueve de la carretera TO-1375, no fuera un león sino un mastín tibetano. Estos perros presentan un aspecto relativamente similar al de los leones y no se descarta que exista una confusión. La llamada al servicio de emergencias 112 se produjo el miércoles y desde entonces los vecinos de la zona están muy pendientes de la evolución de la situación.

articles.title: Dos detenidos tras confirmarse el crimen de Sonia Bellina, la joven que apareció calcinada en un viñedo en Nîmes
articles.standfirst: La mujer de 29 años desapareció el pasado 10 de agosto y su cuerpo fue localizado desnudo
articles.summary: La mujer de 29 años desapareció el pasado 10 de agosto y su cuerpo fue localizado desnudo
articles.body: La Fiscalía de Nîmes ha confirmado que el cadáver parcialmente calcinado encontrado hace unos días en unos viñedos de Saint-Gilles, en el sur de Francia, pertenece a Sonia Bellina, una ‘influencer’ francesa de 29 años. La investigación por el crimen continúa abierta y, por el momento, hay dos personas detenidas como sospechosas del crimen. El cuerpo de la joven fue localizado por un agricultor en una zona de viñedos y, según las primeras informaciones, se encontraba desnudo y con marcas de haber sido parcialmente calcinado. La identidad de la víctima ha podido ser confirmada después de que las autoridades realizaran las correspondientes pruebas de ADN. Bellina vivía entre París y Nîmes y contaba con una gran comunidad de seguidores en redes sociales. Su cuenta principal de TikTok acumulaba alrededor de 260.000 seguidores, mientras que en Instagram reunía cerca de 13.000 seguidores. La hermana de Sonia Bellina explicó a la Policía que la última vez que vio con vida a la joven fue el pasado 10 de agosto, hace más de una semana. En aquel momento, la influencer le habría contado que tenía previsto verse con una persona entre los días 11 y 12 de agosto. A partir de ese momento, sus familiares perdieron el contacto con ella y comenzaron las labores de búsqueda para tratar de localizarla. Días después, el hallazgo del cadáver en Saint-Gilles abrió una investigación policial que finalmente ha permitido confirmar que se trataba de la joven influencer desaparecida. Las autoridades francesas mantienen abiertas varias líneas de investigación para esclarecer las causas de la muerte y determinar la implicación de los dos detenidos en el crimen. Por ahora, la Fiscalía de Nîmes no ha dado más detalles sobre su identidad ni sobre los posibles motivos del crimen. La familia de Bellina también ha denunciado el acoso que ha sufrido desde que se conoció la desaparición de la joven. Su hermana aseguró al medio Midi Libre que han recibido mensajes muy duros durante estos días. "Hay mensajes horribles dirigidos contra Sonia", explicó.

articles.title: Melania Trump announces new foster scholarships ahead of IndyCar DC event
articles.summary: First lady Melania Trump announced a new round of scholarships for foster children Thursday in partnership with IndyCar and Fox Corporation. articles.body:
First lady Melania Trump announced a new round of scholarships for foster children Thursday in partnership with IndyCar and Fox Corporation.

The two companies donated $2 million to fund scholarships at Indiana and Purdue Universities.

“Tomorrow’s leaders are sitting in classrooms today, including those growing up in foster care. Their capability is no less remarkable,” the first lady said during the event in the White House’s Rose Garden.

“Fostering the Future elevates America’s youth based on merit and talent, lifting them beyond economic circumstance and every other condition that may limit opportunity,” she added.

The announcement comes ahead of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix race through Washington on Sunday.

The first lady was presented with a specially designed helmet by IndyCar’s drivers. It is red, white and blue with a star on top, along with her name and “BE BEST” and “Fostering the Future” inscribed on it.

“Thinking about the young people that are here today, they’re going to be the benefactors, have an education, build a career, and I might say, many of them might be the leaders of our country and our business,” said Roger Penske, founder and chair of the Penske Corporation and owner of IndyCar.

The first lady has been a big advocate for children in foster care. She launched Fostering the Future in 2021, an initiative that focuses on supporting educational opportunities for children in foster care.

It’s part of her broader “BE BEST” initiative launched during President Trump’s first term. Fostering the Future is now part of 26 colleges and universities around the country.

President Trump signed an executive order last November that advanced Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future initiatives.

And earlier this year, she lobbied Congress to pass a set of bipartisan reforms that would modernize a program for young people transitioning out of the foster system.

The House Ways and Means Committee has been pushing for legislation to modernize the Chafee program, which helps foster youth aged 14-21 who have aged out of the program.

The proposals would focus on the state utilization of Chafee funds; expand education, training opportunities and access to legal services; and improve support for foster youth that are or about to become parents.

“New legislation for the foster care community is a moral imperative,” Melania Trump said earlier this year. “Beginning here in this room, we can once again change people’s lives. With the new legislation, we can ensure that the opportunity is more than helpful for individuals in the foster care community. It can be their birthright.”

The legislation passed the House in May but has yet to be passed in the Senate.

Marc Beckman, senior adviser to the first lady, told USA Today that Melania Trump is “personally involved” in calling on Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and “trying to get him to force a vote because it was passed infamously in the House.

“She is working behind the scenes,” he added.

articles.title: All red states should immediately audit their biggest school districts
articles.summary: At the end of June, an audit of Jefferson County Public Schools was released to the public. The largest district in Kentucky, Jefferson County (which includes Louisville) enrolls almost 100,000 students — one in seven students in the state. The report by auditor Allison Ball reveals the system’s complete institutional failure. In 2024, Kentucky House…
articles.body:
At the end of June, an audit of Jefferson County Public Schools was released to the public. The largest district in Kentucky, Jefferson County (which includes Louisville) enrolls almost 100,000 students — one in seven students in the state.

The report by auditor Allison Ball reveals the system’s complete institutional failure.

In 2024, Kentucky House Bill 6 compelled a special examination of Jefferson County schools and provided the funds to do so. Over the course of a few months, the auditing team reviewed over 2,000 documents from the 2022 through 2025 school years, visited schools, surveyed websites, and facilitated thousands of focus groups, interviews, and surveys.

The investigation reveals financial mismanagement, administrative bloat, and a school district without a clear direction, purpose or plan.

Reading the nearly 500-page report, what strikes one first is the flood of cash in which the district is drowning. Over 20 years, the per-pupil revenue has risen 62 percent, adjusted for inflation. Over the last decade, the school board approved the maximum property tax increase every single year. The report veers into exasperated disbelief when Ball writes that, despite receiving a bonus $500 million in additional funds during COVID, the district “somehow began running a budget deficit.”

Meanwhile, only 32 percent of elementary students scored as proficient readers on standardized tests. Did the money go to teachers? Nope. The average teacher salary has only increased by 12 percent over two decades.

In Ball’s words , the district has “a spending, not a revenue, problem.”

The list of concerns in the report is long. The district lacks a current and cohesive plan. Its board operates with too little focus on student outcomes. Twenty-six percent of its schools are under-enrolled. One fifth of all its students feel unsafe at school.

Stakeholders reported concerns about limited transparency and lack of input on the board’s decisions. Some teachers appeared uncertain or lacked clarity regarding curriculum content. The district has $1.3 billion in unmet facilities needs. For the 2022-23 and 2024-25 school years, 33,358 behavior incidents on buses were committed by repeat offenders — 78 percent of all such incidents.

Some of the most damning points in the report are the most prosaic. For example, no policy requires a written bid before the district enters into contracts with vendors.

By the end of the report, the reader is left with the impression that this district is filled with individuals with no clue how to manage the state’s largest school system.

This is not just a matter of woke Marxists trying to indoctrinate your children. Rather, it is an assemblage of mediocre to incompetent staff with no concept of governance, tradeoffs or management involved in running an organization. If this were a business, every single administrator in the school district would probably be fired, and the district would perform better as a result.

A district-wide breakdown such as this does not occur in a vacuum. Nor is this problem isolated to one school system in one state. Rather, a number of incentives and first principles make such systemic failure a norm in public K-12 education.

A refusal to acknowledge tradeoffs and limitations (a school cannot be all things to all students) means that districts chase too many goals and extend their resources far beyond their reasonable capacities. Traditional pipelines for leadership — from teacher to principal to district administrator — reward instructional excellence. But institutional leadership requires a different skillset from that of an excellent educator.

Despite financial mismanagement, an ever-increasing budget only rewards fiscal irresponsibility. Top-heavy personnel trees mean vampiric district offices suck away resources from schools before funds reach the classroom, teachers, and students.

These systemic issues are far too numerous for any one policy to fix. There is no one standardized test, curriculum, school choice policy, or funding formula that will shift all incentives, change all minds, and suddenly develop the operational excellence necessary to run a complex school system.

What are the answers? Well, there is fiscal austerity, strengthened personnel pipelines, better curriculum, increased accountability, slashed regulations and smarter pay structures, to name just a few. And notably, although I love highfalutin calls for a return to classical education and debates over first principles, this audit suggests a need for something much simpler first: a development of competence.

Can schools even keep the trains running on time, professional roles clarified and teachers knowledgeable of their curriculum?

A sober, comprehensive audit such as this one should be conducted everywhere. It provides an unsparing look into school districts’ straits, thereby emphasizing the need for comprehensive reform beyond mere funding increases. In fact, a thorough analysis of the report suggests that another blank check will only make matters worse — the same way another hit of a drug relieves symptoms in the moment but worsens addiction.

This audit lists not only complaints, but also recommendations for improvement.

Were every red state in the country to compel such audits of their largest school systems, the vastness of public education’s failures would become apparent. Pat answers would no longer suffice. Systemic failure requires comprehensive reform. The findings of this audit would be difficult for any district to face, but kudos to Kentucky for being willing at least to acknowledge them.

Other states would be wise to do the same.

Daniel Buck is a research fellow and the director of the Conservative Education Reform Network at the American Enterprise Institute.

articles.title: Trump administration wants to deny ABA ability to oversee law schools: Report
articles.summary: The Department of Education has suggested ending the American Bar Association’s (ABA) oversight on the law school accreditation process. The ABA has had the power to accredit nearly 200 law schools over the last 70 years, but this power may come to an end, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The department made its…
articles.body:
The Department of Education has suggested ending the American Bar Association’s (ABA) oversight on the law school accreditation process.

The ABA has had the power to accredit nearly 200 law schools over the last 70 years, but this power may come to an end, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The department made its first official move to limit the association’s power on Friday.

Assistant Education Secretary David Barker told the Journal that he sees the accreditation process “like a cartel,” as many of these oversight agencies lack competition. He added that the model allows accreditors to “feel free to inject their own political preferences.”

Chair of the ABA’s Accreditation Council Melissa Hart wrote in a statement to the Journal that the Education Department’s move was “one step in the regular recognition process that the Council and other accreditors periodically complete.”

“A hearing is the next step in that process, and we’re confident the Council will address any concerns the Department may have at that hearing,” she added.

The accreditation process acts as an educational quality check that also determines whether students at a given higher education institution will have access to federal loans. In many states, a law student who did not attend an ABA-accredited program cannot take the bar exam.

The ABA and Department of Education did not immediately respond to The Hill’s request for comment.

This attack to the ABA’s power falls within a broader pattern within the Trump administration, as officials continue to leverage grants and government funding to keep educational institutions on a short leash.

In March, for example, The Department of Education announced it would investigate more than 50 colleges and universities over alleged “racial preferences” in admissions and academics.

The ABA similarly faced pressure in May to roll back Standard 206, which stated law schools desiring accreditation must “demonstrate by concrete action a commitment to diversity and inclusion.”

Republicans have also accused the association of harboring left-leaning political biases. In late 2025, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier (R) referred to the ABA as an arm of a political left-wing party.”

In February 2025, Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson barred political appointees from renewing their ABA membership, writing in a letter to staff that the association “advances radical left-wing causes and promotes the business interests of Big Tech.”

articles.summary: Education Secretary Linda McMahon said Sunday her department is “cracking down” on K-12 teachers sexually harassing students. During an interview on CNN’s “State of the Union,” McMahon criticized the practice of a school district reassigning a teacher accused of sexually harassing a student to another school. “And it’s not part of their record or anything,…
articles.body:
Education Secretary Linda McMahon said Sunday her department is “cracking down” on K-12 teachers sexually harassing students.

During an interview on CNN’s “State of the Union,” McMahon criticized the practice of a school district reassigning a teacher accused of sexually harassing a student to another school.

“And it’s not part of their record or anything, so we have really been cracking down on that as well,” she told host Dana Bash.

McMahon also noted that 1 in 10 children will be sexually molested by the time they finish high school, citing research her department conducted.

ProPublica and KQED reported in May that the state of California did not revoke the professional licenses of 67 teachers whom school districts determined sexually harassed students or committed other types of sexual misconduct from 2019 through 2025.

Other schools hired at least 14 of those educators, with at least 12 of those still working in education as of May, according to the reporting.

The Education Department responded to that reporting by launching an investigation into the Los Angeles Unified School District, as well as a nationwide effort to “crack down” on teachers harassing students.

The former probe centers on the district’s alleged agreement with the United Teachers of Los Angeles union that it will reassign — and not terminate — teachers that are credibly accused of having a sexual or romantic relationship with a student, creating child pornography and failing to report suspected child abuse, according to a letter McMahon penned to educational institutions in July.

In the letter, McMahon noted the Education Department can revoke federal funding from schools that do not comply with federal sexual misconduct laws.

“Make no mistake, the Department will fully enforce federal law and employ every resource at its disposal to protect children from sexual predators,” the Education secretary wrote. “Those schools that allow sexual misconduct to occur risk the termination of applicable federal assistance provided by the federal government.”

“This epidemic of nationwide sexual abuse in our schools must end.”

articles.title: American Federation of Teachers launches boycott against Target, claims retailer 'remained silent' on ICE
articles.summary: Randi Weingarten launched an AFT back-to-school boycott of Target over ICE silence, but critics say pension fund leverage warrants a federal probe.
articles.body: American Federation of Teachers (AFT) President Randi Weingarten promoted a nationwide back-to-school boycott of retail giant Target over the weekend because the company had not condemned ICE operations in Minnesota — the location of its headquarters — prompting criticism from education advocates and a call for federal scrutiny. "We gave Target ample time to stand with the communities in which they operate and help their neighbors, but its silence about federal immigration abuses has been deafening," Weingarten said in a statement. "The issue could not be more pressing: Seven months since the murders of Alex Pretti and Renée Good, masked ICE agents are still in our streets, our schools and our communities, terrorizing families in the name of Donald Trump’s illegal and immoral assault on immigrants striving for their American Dream," she continued. "That’s why we’re urging our members to avoid Target and patronize more ethical shopping alternatives this back-to-school season." Weingarten also shared a video on Instagram, where she directed families to the AFT’s "Shop Smart, Not Target" website, which maps local back-to-school shopping alternatives. The organization launched the campaign Wednesday after sending Target CEO Michael Fiddelke letters in February and March. WATCH: WEINGARTEN GESTURES WILDLY DURING ANTI-TRUMP RANT, LATER SAYS HE DRIVES HER TO DRINK Corey DeAngelis, a Heritage Foundation research fellow, told Fox News Digital Sunday that using the organization’s pension influence against Target raised fiduciary concerns and warranted a federal investigation. "This partisan war on Target smells like a breach of fiduciary duty given that AFT members’ pension funds own 6.79 million shares of Target stock, which Weingarten has already leveraged to pressure the company into opposing ICE," he said. "The Department of Justice should open an investigation into the AFT using their pension funds and political influence to bully companies into falling in line with their socialist agenda." "Urging educators and families to avoid Target is not an appropriate use of the union’s resources or influence," he added.  This isn't the AFT's first time batting against the retail giant. DeAngelis also supplied Fox News Digital with a chart tracking Target’s closing share price against several AFT actions, including Weingarten’s letters and the organization’s March boycott resolution. TEACHERS UNION FACING YEARS OF DEFICITS SEEKS TO BECOME OREGON'S LARGEST PAC, INTERNAL DOCUMENTS SHOW Sonja Shaw, a candidate for California superintendent of public instruction and Chino Valley Unified School District board president, told Fox News Digital on Sunday that labor leaders were prioritizing political power while students continued to struggle academically. "Teachers’ unions are supposed to fight for teachers. Instead, union leadership has become a political machine obsessed with money, power and influence while our children continue to fall behind," she said. "In California, more than half our students are not proficient in basic reading and math. When a system produces those results year after year, that isn’t success. That’s education malpractice." California's latest statewide assessments showed 48.8% of students met or exceeded English language arts standards and 37.3% met or exceeded math standards. The AFT's March resolution explicitly called the effort a boycott and urged its 1.8 million members, families and allies to avoid Target until the company stood with the Twin Cities. TEXAS’ LARGEST SCHOOL DISTRICT SEES TEST SCORES SOAR AFTER STATE TAKEOVER DESPITE RACISM CLAIMS DeAngelis’ request followed Sen. Eric Schmitt’s, R-Missouri, July appeal for the Labor Department to investigate whether AFT leaders coordinated with retirement-plan fiduciaries to use members’ assets for political objectives. House lawmakers separately demanded answers about reports that member dues helped finance Weingarten’s book, "Why Fascists Fear Teachers," while she received royalties. Teachers spend an average of $895 of their own money every year on supplies their students need, according to a 2025 teacher spending survey. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached to the AFT, DHS, ICE and Target for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: McMahon: AI can be a ‘great tool’ for students
articles.summary: Education Secretary Linda McMahon said Sunday that AI could be a helpful tool for K-12 students if schools and educators apply the technology properly. During an interview on CNN’s “State of the Union,” McMahon spoke of her recent visit to the Alpha School in Austin, Texas. Students at the private institution interact with chatbots for…
articles.body:
Education Secretary Linda McMahon said Sunday that AI could be a helpful tool for K-12 students if schools and educators apply the technology properly.

During an interview on CNN’s “ State of the Union ,” McMahon spoke of her recent visit to the Alpha School in Austin, Texas.

Students at the private institution interact with chatbots for the “first couple of hours” every day, McMahon noted, with teachers “monitoring what they’re doing.”

McMahon told host Dana Bash, “The beauty of that is that a student almost has a one-on-one tutor. So, the teacher can monitor to see if a child is a bit behind and repeat information for them. If a child is really excelling, then their programs get sped up a bit.”

“So it’s a great tool to have in this particular school,” she continued.

Last year, 54 percent of students and 53 percent of English, math and science teachers said they used AI for school, according to a survey conducted by the RAND Corporation. That marked increases of 15-plus percentage points relative to surveys conducted over the prior two years.

Earlier this week, the Education Department released guidance for technology use in the classroom, intended to apply to the use of artificial intelligence and technology writ large.

Kirsten Baesler, the department’s assistant secretary in charge of the Office of Elementary and Education, wrote in a letter to K-12 school leaders that institutions should be “increasingly intentional about the digital experiences” students have access to.

“The effectiveness of any educational technology depends on the quality of the tool, the purpose for which it is used, and the conditions in which it is implemented,” Baesler wrote. “Not only do we need to know if the tool works, but if it works; why does it work, for whom does it work, and under what conditions.”

McMahon echoed her assistant secretary’s letter, saying policymakers and educators have to determine the specific results of increasing artificial intelligence use in the classroom.

“Are we seeing better outcomes in schools? And if we’re not, then … they should be pulled out. But I have seen it work so well in the introductions that I’ve seen,” McMahon said.

She added, “As we introduce it, I think, slowly in schools, it can be a very effective tool used properly.”

McMahon noted, though, that parents “have every right” to opt their children out of AI-centered instruction if they are “not seeing” a positive outcome from the technology’s use.

articles.title: Ten Commandments belong in Texas schools and the Supreme Court can protect them
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court faces a pivotal decision on whether Texas public schools can constitutionally display the Ten Commandments in classrooms.
articles.body: The U.S. Supreme Court has been asked to decide if the Ten Commandments can be posted in Texas public schools. In the coming months, the justices will decide whether or not to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit which found that the posting the Ten Commandments in schools is not only constitutional, but also consistent with America’s historical understanding of religion’s role in public life. Documents and history are not banned in this country because they are religious or have religious content. Are students allowed to read the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr.’s "Letter from Birmingham Jail?" Of course they are. TEXAS BOARD OF EDUCATION APPROVES REQUIRED READING LIST WITH BIBLE PASSAGES FOR 5 MILLION STUDENTS Banning parts of our religious history and heritage is not an act of compliance with the First Amendment. It is hostility to religion and a religious cleansing, foreign to our Constitution. The First Amendment forbids the government from establishing an official state religion — something akin to the Church of England, where the state controlled doctrine, compelled worship and punished dissenters. The Fifth Circuit’s ruling made clear that such "establishments" historically involved acts of coercion such as mandatory church attendance or legal penalties for noncompliance. Displaying a religious text on a classroom wall bears no resemblance to such practices. SUPREME COURT SHOWDOWN LOOMS OVER ST MICHAEL STATUE BLOCKED FROM PUBLIC SAFETY BUILDING The Ten Commandments are a foundational moral, literary and historical text. Their influence on Western legal traditions is widely acknowledged, even by critics. The Commandments articulate basic ethical principles such as prohibitions against murder, theft and perjury that underpin modern legal systems. Displaying them in classrooms is simply a recognition of their historical and cultural significance. A quality education must include instruction on the religious and historical heritage of our country. Without it, students cannot understand the founding rationale of our nation, nor its system of laws. JUDGE ORDERS WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT TO LOOSEN LIMITS ON OFF-CAMPUS BIBLE CLUB FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL STUDENTS Critics argue that posting the Ten Commandments amounts to coercion, especially for impressionable students. But this claim does not withstand scrutiny. The Texas law at issue requires only that a poster be displayed. It does not mandate prayer, belief or participation in any religious activity. Students are not asked to recite the Commandments, affirm their truth or even engage with them at all. In other words, exposure is not indoctrination. This distinction is crucial. Public education inevitably exposes students to a wide range of historical, philosophical, and, yes, religious ideas. The Constitution does not demand that schools become religion-free zones; rather, it protects against government coercion in matters of faith. As the Fifth Circuit notes, "the mere presence of religious language in a school display is [not] ipso facto religious coercion." If it were, many longstanding features of American public life, from the national motto "In God We Trust" to references to a "Creator" in the Declaration of Independence, would be constitutionally suspect. GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS The legal foundation for the Fifth Circuit’s conclusion rests heavily on First Liberty Institute’s victory in Kennedy v. Bremerton School District, which fundamentally reshaped Establishment Clause jurisprudence. As the Fifth Circuit explains, Kennedy abandoned the long-criticized "Lemon test" and replaced it with an approach rooted in "historical practices and understandings." Under this framework, courts no longer ask whether a government action has a secular purpose, but whether it resembles the kinds of coercive religious establishments the Founders sought to prohibit. This shift is decisive: because a classroom display imposes no religious exercise, no punishment for dissent and no government control over belief, it falls far outside the historical definition of an "establishment of religion." In short, Kennedy clarifies that the Constitution protects against coercion, not mere exposure to religious ideas, history and heritage. RARE AMERICAN BIBLE AND FOUNDERS’ LETTERS TRACE FAITH’S ROLE IN BIRTH OF THE NATION The Founders themselves did not envision a strict separation of religion from public education. As Judge James Ho quoted President George Washington in his concurrence, they believed that "religion and morality are indispensable supports" of a free society. Far from excluding religion, early American institutions often incorporated it as a source of moral guidance and civic virtue. Public education inevitably exposes students to a wide range of historical, philosophical, and, yes, religious ideas. articles.body: A Houston Uber driver was caught "off guard" but kept his cool when two police officers jumped into his vehicle and directed him to chase a suspect fleeing on foot, frantic dashcam video shows. Anthony Baines said he was driving for Uber at about 12:20 a.m. Aug. 8 in a Houston Heights neighborhood, when a shirtless man ran across the street in front of his vehicle with two Houston Police Department officers close behind, according to Storyful. The video shows Baines getting waved down by an officer and stopping as she approaches and hops into the front passenger seat. HANDCUFFED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY SLIPS RESTRAINTS, STEALS DALLAS POLICE CRUISER WITH OFFICER TRAPPED IN BACK SEAT "Hey, give me a ride over there please," the officer says in the video. "Go, go that way … go, go, go, go, go!" Baines can be heard asking which way he should drive as officers point him in the direction of the suspect. After driving a short distance, the officer signals for her partner, who's carrying a flashlight, to get in the vehicle, too, and opens the car door and jumps into the backseat. RIDESHARE PASSENGER HELD HOSTAGE FOR EIGHT HOURS DURING ARMED STANDOFF WITH POLICE IN SWANKY NEIGHBORHOOD The officers rode with Baines for several minutes while searching the area before one of them appeared to spot the suspect. Both officers jump out of the Uber and resume their pursuit on foot. "What the f---?!" Baines is heard saying as the officers dart from his car. BODYCAM SHOWS POLICE K-9 LEAPING INTO ACTION AFTER SUSPECTED IMPAIRED DRIVER REFUSED TO SURRENDER "It caught me completely off guard," Baines told Storyful. "I’ve never had anything like that happen driving. I was surprised but just did what the officer asked in the moment." Houston police confirmed the authenticity of the video and the incident to KPRC 2, which reported officers had been responding to a terroristic threat call involving allegations that the suspect threatened to shoot a woman and her children after becoming upset over a belief that someone had stolen from him. Police said officers tried to detain the man as he left an apartment, but he refused to cooperate and ran away. An officer asked the driver to take them around the block to the apartment complex, where the officers returned to their own vehicle, according to KPRC. FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED IN IHOP RESTAURANT AFTER POLICE SAY HE STABBED A RIDESHARE DRIVER Despite the unusual assistance, police did not locate the suspect. His identity has not been released, and the investigation remains ongoing. Baines later appeared to confirm in a social media post that he was the Uber driver behind the dashcam footage. "Yep, that was me," he wrote. "The Uber driver whose dashcam caught two HPD officers jumping in my car to chase a suspect." articles.title: Muere una niña de ocho años infectada por la parásito 'comecerebros': pudo contagiarse mientras se bañaba en un lago
articles.standfirst: El hecho se produjo en Louisiana
articles.summary: El hecho se produjo en Louisiana
articles.body: Una niña de ocho años ha fallecido en Louisiana (Estados Unidos) tras contraer una extraña infección causada por la ameba Naegleria fowleri, conocida popularmente como la "ameba comecerebros". Según las autoridades sanitarias, la menor pudo haberse contagiado del parásito microscópico mientras se bañaba en un lago cercano a su domicilio. La víctima, Lillian Smart, vecina de Ruston, moría en un hospital apenas un día después de celebrar su octavo cumpleaños. La noticia fue confirmada por su familia a través de una publicación en redes sociales, recogida posteriormente por medios como CNN y The Guardian. "Anoche Lillian pasó de nuestros brazos a los brazos de Jesús", escribió su familia. "Las lesiones en su cerebro eran demasiado graves para que su pequeño cuerpo pudiera recuperarse. Todos hicieron todo lo posible por salvarla. Estamos destrozados y no sabemos cómo seguir adelante", añadieron. El Departamento de Salud de Louisiana informó el pasado 19 de agosto de un caso de infección por Naegleria fowleri en un residente del estado, cuya exposición al organismo se habría producido durante un baño en el lago Claiborne, situado a unos 48 kilómetros al noroeste de Ruston. Aunque las autoridades no revelaron inicialmente la identidad de la paciente, familiares y allegados confirmaron después a medios locales que se trataba de Lillian. Se trata de un organismo microscópico que habita en aguas dulces cálidas, como lagos, ríos y estanques. La infección se produce cuando el agua contaminada entra por la nariz, permitiendo que la ameba alcance el cerebro. Una vez allí, puede provocar una meningoencefalitis amebiana primaria, una enfermedad extremadamente rara, pero con una tasa de mortalidad muy elevada. Aunque los casos son poco frecuentes, las autoridades sanitarias recuerdan que el riesgo aumenta durante los meses más cálidos y recomiendan extremar las precauciones en aguas dulces templadas o calientes, especialmente al bucear o realizar actividades que favorezcan la entrada de agua por las fosas nasales.

articles.title: What Megan Rapinoe gets wrong in the transgender athlete debate
articles.summary: Rapinoe says girls can speak for ourselves, but she dismisses the girls who do.
articles.body:
Megan Rapinoe recently wrote in an op-ed that women and girls “can speak for ourselves.” As two female high school athletes living under Washington state’s current sports policies, we could not agree more.

Here is what’s happening in Washington: One of us finished second in a girls’ 1600-meter state race, behind a biological male. The other sat out of a girls’ basketball game rather than play against a biological male on the opposing team.

We wanted the same thing every girl athlete wants: a fair and safe chance to compete in the sports we love. We were both denied that.

Our decision to speak up has been costly. We have been called hateful, transphobic, bigots and bullies. We have both been harassed online and in person. One of us was told she would be responsible if transgender athletes take their own lives because we spoke up. One of us was even sued for speaking publicly about what happened.

All of this for demanding that girls receive fair competition, privacy and equal opportunities.

That is why Rapinoe’s essay is so frustrating. She says girls can speak for ourselves, but she dismisses the girls who do.

We respect what Rapinoe accomplished on the soccer field. She helped grow women’s sports and spent her career fighting for better pay and recognition for female athletes. But her whole career was built inside a protected category for women only. She never had to win a spot on a sex-neutral national team.

Rapinoe was able to compete against other women because the leagues she played in understood that sex matters in athletic competition — the very thing she now says should not matter. It is easy for her to tell high school girls to accept policies she never had to compete under herself.

That is why the claims about Washington’s Initiative 638 matter. Rapinoe’s most alarming one is that Initiative 638 would force girls to undergo genital inspections or buy DNA or hormone tests before they can play. That is simply false. The initiative, which will appear on Washington state ballots this fall, would simply require students competing in female-only sports to provide a statement from their own health care providers verifying biological sex, as part of the sports physical they already complete. The provider can rely on existing records or patient history to do it.

Doctors in Washington already use internal forms that include sex verification. Those forms stay with the doctor instead of appearing on the sports physical sheet. So Initiative 638 merely adds a check box for a doctor to fill out on a form that already exists.

Rapinoe asks whether girls who are tall, muscular, fast, short-haired, or deep-voiced will count as “girl enough.” Of course a girl can be tall, strong, short-haired, or have interests that don’t fit expectations. None of that makes her any less of a female. Keeping girls in girls’ leagues and boys in boys’ leagues has nothing to do with how feminine or masculine anyone looks. It has to do with their sex.

Rapinoe remembers being a 13-year-old who didn’t fit someone else’s idea of femininity. We both understand why that memory matters to her. But Initiative 638 would never have asked whether she looked feminine enough. Rather it would have recognized that she was female and therefore eligible for the category that allowed her to become a World Cup champion.

People often say there are so few transgender athletes competing that girls should just accept the current policies. But Washington does not even know how many biological males are competing in girls’ sports. One of us had already competed against four different biological males by her sophomore year. Our state superintendent explained that the WIAA’s reported numbers only count transgender athletes at the varsity level. Everyone competing below varsity is left out.

For girls, the loss of even one lost roster spot, championship, scholarship or fair shot against a male athlete is already one too many.

This is not about hatred or denying anyone’s dignity. Transgender students deserve respect, privacy and protection from harassment. Every student should have a real chance to participate in sports. But respect for one group should not come at the expense of another. Protecting transgender students does not require girls to give up the fairness and safety that sex-based categories in sports were created to provide. Washington can and should do both.

We do not want Rapinoe to stop speaking. We are asking her to stop dismissing girls who disagree with her, treating them like they are invisible and claiming they are hateful or being manipulated. When she does that, she fuels hostility and makes it harder for girls to tell their stories without fear. Listening to girls means listening to all girls, even the ones who disagree.

We are speaking for ourselves, and we will not quit.

Frances Staudt and Ahnaleigh Wilson are high school athletes in Washington state.

articles.title: Jury convicts Kevin Salazar in execution-style killing of LA Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer
articles.summary: Kevin Salazar was convicted of murdering Los Angeles County deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer in a 2023 drive-by ambush near his Palmdale station.
articles.body: A California man has been convicted in the drive-by ambush of a Los Angeles deputy shot and killed at a red light just steps from the sheriff's Palmdale station in 2023. Jurors found Kevin Salazar, 32, guilty of the murder of Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer Monday after a week-long trial. "It’s very helpful that the justice system prevail, that you have a conviction that is a benefit to the family," Brad Gage, the Los Angeles attorney representing Clinkunbroomer's family, told Fox News Digital. "That gives some solace. That gives some comfort." MURDERED LOS ANGELES SHERIFF'S DEPUTY'S FAMILY SLAPS COUNTY WITH $20M WRONGFUL DEATH LAWSUIT Around 6 p.m. on Sept. 16, 2023, Clinkunbroomer pulled up to a red light down the street from the sheriff's station in Palmdale. He was driving his marked car and wearing his uniform. As he waited for the light to turn green, another car pulled up alongside him – and a man inside shot him in the head. Authorities said Salazar had followed Clinkunbroomer from the Palmdale Sheriff's Station to the intersection less than a block away before opening fire with a .22 revolver. He sped off, and Clinkunbroomer was pronounced dead at a hospital. Authorities found Salazar at his family's home in Palmdale two days later and arrested him on murder charges after a standoff, part of which was caught on video. ARREST MADE IN AMBUSH KILLING OF LA SHERIFF'S DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER Clinkunbroomer, 30, was engaged to be married at the time of his murder. "When a parent loses a child, there’s no name for it," Gage said. "It’s so painful, it’s so traumatic, it is so devastating that it is beyond words." Jurors deliberated for just 2 1/2 hours before finding Salazar guilty of first-degree murder as well as the special circumstance allegations of murder of a peace officer, lying in wait and firing from a vehicle, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office. WATCH: Suspect arrested following fatal shooting of LA sheriff’s deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer Despite the conviction, a motive remains unclear, according to the family's attorney. "As far as we know, there was no reason," Gage told Fox News Digital. "It was just execution of a police officer." The court will move on Wednesday to a sanity-deciding phase for Salazar, to determine whether he goes to prison or is confined in a state mental hospital after he raised an insanity defense. SEND US A TIP "This brutal and senseless murder took the life of a dedicated deputy, leaving his family, colleagues and community to endure an unimaginable loss. We hope today’s guilty verdict brings a measure of healing to Deputy Clinkunbroomer’s family and loved ones," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said in a statement. Clinkunbroomer came from a law enforcement family. His grandfather, father and brother all served. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Ryan dedicated his life to service, proudly carrying on his family’s legacy as a third-generation member of the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department," Sheriff Robert Luna said after the verdict. "We will forever honor his service, his sacrifice and the badge he proudly wore. Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer will never be forgotten." After his death, the family sued the county, alleging that mandatory overtime and understaffing had left Clinkunbroomer exhausted and more vulnerable to the ambush, Gage said. articles.title: Parents are winning — and the Department of Education is leading the charge
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Education and the Department of Justice have intensified enforcement of parental rights laws against school districts that hide student information from parents regarding gender identity and privacy violations.
articles.body:
It’s back-to-school season. And this year, parents have a lot more to celebrate than just the excitement of fresh school supplies and predictable schedules.

Parents across America have been sidelined , silenced and shut out of their children’s education for too long. Records have been hidden. Administrators have stonewalled . Parents have been treated as obstacles rather than partners.

But today, the tide has turned — and the U.S. Department of Education deserves some credit for the pro-parent momentum.

This administration has done something commendable: It has taken existing federal parental rights laws — laws that sat unenforced for years while school districts brazenly ignored them — and enforced them with teeth. Something past administrations wouldn’t even consider, much less do. The result has been authentic investigations, real consequences and needed accountability. Finally, parents are being heard, and schools are taking notice.

In just one week surrounding National Parents’ Day on July 26, the department stood firmly with parents and held schools to account.

It launched a crackdown on school districts that have been facilitating students adopting new so-called gender identities at school (with different names and wrong-sex pronouns) — all while actively concealing it from their own parents.

It opened new parental rights investigations into Denver Public Schools in Colorado and Bethel School District in Washington for possible violations of the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment of 1978.

It found that the Burlington Public Schools in Massachusetts violated the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment when it forced students to take a “Youth Risk Behavior Survey” — a sexually explicit survey from which many parents had expressly opted their children out.

And it demanded that California and Washington explain their policies pressuring schools to hide student records and vital information from parents — policies so egregious they triggered the department’s first-ever statewide Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974 investigations.

That is not just a bureaucracy in motion. That is a Department of Education with a backbone.

And the department has taken specific and decisive enforcement actions to preserve parental rights. In partnership with the U.S. Department of Justice, it took enforcement action against Anne Arundel County, Md. schools after finding the district hid students’ transgender identity from parents by improperly classifying it as “confidential medical information.”

In Ann Arbor, Mich., the department determined the district’s policy directing employees to hide children’s transgender identity from parents likely violates the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act and threatened enforcement. In Kansas City, Kan., a school district repeatedly refused to come into voluntary compliance with the law and stop hiding this same information. The Department of Education and Department of Justice therefore announced it would pursue judicial proceedings and the potential loss of federal funding.

The message is clear : The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act is not an optional statute. It is the law. Districts that lie to parents and hide sensitive information about their child are on notice that federal enforcement action is coming — and fast.

Earlier this year, the U.S. Department of Education issued a finding against the California Department of Education, which has been hiding information from parents in what it calls “gender support plans.” California had also asked its student data management company to conceal name and pronoun changes from parents.

And at the beginning of summer, the red tape was cut. The Department of Education and Department of Justice formalized an interagency agreement to “expedite enforcement of our nation’s parental and civil rights laws.” In other words, enforcement of pro-parent laws is finally a priority.

This much-needed momentum is also being reinforced by the courts. In Mirabelli v. Bonta , the U.S. Supreme Court reaffirmed that it is parents, not government, who have “primary authority” over their children’s education and upbringing. And the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit quickly followed suit in June 2026, holding that California laws forbidding schools from notifying parents when their child socially transitions to a new gender identities at school likely violates parents’ constitutional rights.

Educational freedom is also being expanded. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act established a federal education tax credit scholarship program for the first time. The program provides for a dollar-for-dollar tax credit of up to $1,700 for individual donations to Scholarship Granting Organizations that provide K-12 student scholarships for low- and middle-income families.

Thirty-one states have already announced plans to opt in to this historic program, starting Jan. 1, 2027. Parents will be empowered to choose what is best for their children’s education, aligned with their family values and their children’s unique needs. These new scholarships will now be available to an estimated 90 percent of K-12 students nationwide.

This is what it looks like when the federal government stands with parents instead of against them. Preserving parental rights through enforcement. Protecting through policies that empower.

The message for school districts is simple: Hide information from parents, and your federal funding is at risk. The message to parents is even simpler: Keep fighting. We’re winning.

Kate Anderson serves as senior counsel and director of the Center for Parental Rights at Alliance Defending Freedom .

articles.title: Incendio en Barcelona: 35 hectáreas de Collserola afectadas y dos barrios confinados
articles.standfirst: Los vecinos de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró han recibido un mensaje de ES-Alert
articles.summary: Los vecinos de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró han recibido un mensaje de ES-Alert
articles.body: Un incendio en el parque Collserola (Barcelona) originado alrededor de las 15:30 horas ha obligado a las autoridades a confinar los barrios de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró, en los que viven unas 15.000 personas. "Se ordena el confinamiento de la población de los barrios de Torre Baró y Ciutat Meridiana debido al incendio de vegetación. Cierren puertas y ventanas, detengan los sistemas de ventilación y no salgan a la calle", puede leerse en el texto recibido. De forma preventiva, las autoridades también han desalojado a los vecinos de las calles Castellví y Lliçà del barrio de Torre Baró. Son las dos que están más cerca del incendio. Las autoridades han mandado dos mensajes ES-Alert. El primero, a las 16:45 horas, indicando el confinamiento. El segundo, a las 18:30, en el que se ha insistido en respetar las instrucciones de las autoridades y mantener el civismo en esta situación delicada. El humo se ha visto desde varias zonas de la ciudad y el teléfono de emergencias (112) ha recibido más de mil llamadas de aviso. El incendio afecta a un total de 35 hectáreas, según los datos provisionales ofrecidos por Agents Rurals. Por su parte, Bomberos de la Generalitat ha informado que un total de 160 efectivos y 60 dotaciones, doce aéreas, están trabajando activamente en la zona. Por el momento, las autoridades desconocen el origen del incendio. El fuego se ha iniciado en una zona de matorrales de la carretera alta de Roquetes, en el distrito de Nou Barris y avanza hacia Sant Cugat del Vallès y Cerdanyola del Vallès. Sergi Bové, jefe de intervención de Bomberos de Barcelona, ha atendido a los medios alrededor de las 19:30 horas: "Esperamos que la situación mejore ambientalmente en las próximas horas y podamos controlar los flancos, que es lo que nos preocupa. Lo que debemos de procurar es que no se produzca un cambio de condiciones peor por la noche, un cambio de viento, y que se descontrolen los dos flancos. No podemos dar ninguna previsión". El alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, presente en la zona, ha agradecido el trabajo de bomberos y el resto de autoridades en el incendio. "Como alcalde, pido que se sigan los consejos de Protección Civil. Esperamos que en las próximas horas todo pueda estar controlado. articles.title: ICE lodges detainer for illegal immigrant with lengthy rap sheet after alleged jealousy-fueled killing
articles.summary: ON FOX: Federal immigration officials lodged an ice detainer for a Cuban citizen with drug trafficking convictions charged with second-degree murder.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Federal immigration officials are asking authorities in the Miami area to honor a detainer request for an illegal immigrant with a lengthy criminal history who is now charged with fatally shooting a man on the street in an alleged act of jealousy. William Serrano Domenech, 49, is being held in a Miami-Dade County jail in connection with the Aug. 17 murder of 42-year-old Raul Aballe, the Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday. "He has a rap sheet a mile long, with prior convictions in Florida and Michigan for drug trafficking and illegal possession of a firearm, as well as prior arrests in New Mexico and Tennessee for aggravated assault, theft, and resisting arrest," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This dangerous criminal should have never been in our country, and had it not been for the Biden Administration releasing him from ICE custody in 2023, Raul Aballe would still be alive." EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE Domenech, a Cuban citizen, was "socializing with the witness" on the evening of the slaying when Aballe appeared and the pair began arguing, authorities said. The dispute turned physical when Domenech started punching and slapping Aballe, authorities said. Domenech allegedly pulled a gun out of a fanny pack and opened fire, striking Aballe in the stomach. Aballe was taken to a hospital where he later died. ICE LODGES DETAINER ON SALVADORAN NATIONAL, 18, ACCUSED OF 2 FATAL SHOOTINGS IN HOUSTON Domenech allegedly fled the scene, but he was arrested the next day. He allegedly admitted to the killing and said he was jealous of Aballe's relationship with the witness, according to authorities. The witness reportedly told investigators that Aballe was not armed and didn't initiate the fight. HOW A NONCITIZEN SUSPECTED KILLER GOT CAUGHT AND RELEASED BY NEWSOM-APPOINTED JUDGE: TIMELINE Domenech is charged with second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer with Miami-Dade authorities the day after Domenech's arrest. His criminal history spans at least four states for a litany of offenses, DHS said. That includes a conviction for a weapons offense and arrests on charges of vehicle theft, burglary, driving without a license, and driving with a suspended license in Florida, as well as prior arrests on charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, false imprisonment, and bribery of a witness in New Mexico. HUNDREDS OF JAILED ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED BACK ONTO BLUE-STATE STREETS DESPITE ICE DETAINERS, RECORDS SHOW In addition, Domenech has prior arrests for unlawful possession of a weapon, resisting arrest, and theft in Tennessee, and convictions for possession with intent to distribute five grams or more of cocaine, possession with intent to distribute an unknown quantity of marijuana, possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, possession of a firearm by an illegal alien, and felon in possession of a firearm in Michigan, authorities said. Domenech allegedly told authorities he entered the United States through Florida in 1995. A deportation order was issued by a judge in 2002. ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS However, when ICE took him into custody in 2023, he was released back onto the streets by the Biden administration, DHS said.
