articles.title: Zenón de Citio, filósofo: “La naturaleza nos ha dado dos oídos y una boca para enseñarnos que vale más oír que hablar”
articles.standfirst: El fundador del estoicismo dejó una enseñanza que siglos después sigue presente en la forma de entender la comunicación, la humildad y el pensamiento racional.
articles.summary: El fundador del estoicismo dejó una enseñanza que siglos después sigue presente en la forma de entender la comunicación, la humildad y el pensamiento racional.
articles.body: En un mundo donde las opiniones suelen aparecer antes que la reflexión, una frase atribuida a Zenón de Citio, fundador de la escuela estoica, mantiene vigencia como una invitación a recuperar el valor de la escucha. El filósofo griego, nacido en Citio, Chipre, desarrolló una corriente basada en la razón, la virtud y la búsqueda de una vida en consonancia con la naturaleza. “La naturaleza nos ha dado dos oídos y una boca para enseñarnos que vale más oír que hablar”, es una de las reflexiones más conocidas asociadas a Zenón y resume una parte esencial del pensamiento estoico: controlar los impulsos, analizar antes de actuar y comprender a los demás antes de emitir un juicio. Para los seguidores del estoicismo, la sabiduría no sólo estaba relacionada con acumular conocimiento, sino con aplicar la razón en la vida cotidiana. Escuchar, observar y pensar eran pasos necesarios para alcanzar virtudes como la justicia, la templanza, el coraje y la prudencia. La filosofía de Zenón de Citio colocaba a la razón como una guía para enfrentar las emociones, los deseos y las dificultades de la vida. Desde esa perspectiva, hablar menos y escuchar más no significaba permanecer en silencio, sino actuar con mayor conciencia. Datos clave del pensamiento estoico: La frase sobre los dos oídos y una boca refleja la importancia de la escucha activa. Para Zenón, una persona debía recibir información, analizarla y después responder, evitando actuar únicamente desde la emoción o el impulso. La historia de Zenón estuvo marcada por una transformación personal. Antes de convertirse en filósofo, era comerciante, pero un naufragio cambió el rumbo de su vida y lo llevó hacia una existencia enfocada en la reflexión y el conocimiento. Después de esa experiencia llegó a Atenas, donde comenzó su formación filosófica y posteriormente creó la escuela estoica, llamada así porque sus enseñanzas se impartían en la Stoa Poikilé, un pórtico público de la ciudad. Su pensamiento defendía que el ser humano debía vivir de acuerdo con la naturaleza y aceptar aquello que no podía controlar. La voluntad, la disciplina y el dominio de las pasiones eran elementos centrales para alcanzar una vida más tranquila. Entre sus reflexiones también destaca la idea de aprovechar el tiempo presente: “No obres como si fueras a vivir mil años, obra como si el fin estuviera muy cerca”, una enseñanza relacionada con la importancia de actuar correctamente mientras se tiene la oportunidad. Aunque nació hace más de dos mil años, el estoicismo continúa siendo estudiado por su enfoque sobre la inteligencia emocional, la resiliencia y la manera de enfrentar los problemas cotidianos. La idea de escuchar antes de hablar mantiene relevancia en las relaciones personales, el trabajo y la convivencia social. Para Zenón y otros filósofos estoicos, como Epicteto y Marco Aurelio, comprender el entorno era indispensable para actuar de manera justa. La corriente estoica sostenía que todas las personas forman parte de un mismo sistema llamado naturaleza y que una vida buena depende de encontrar armonía con ese orden. Bajo esa visión, escuchar no sólo es una muestra de respeto, sino una forma de adquirir conocimiento y tomar mejores decisiones.

articles.title: Mystery trio in headlamps and overalls emerges from Manhattan manhole, prompting NYPD probe
articles.summary: The NYPD is reviewing surveillance video after three people in overalls and headlamps were caught emerging from a Manhattan manhole near Penn Station.
articles.body: The New York Police Department is investigating after video showing three people in overalls and headlamps emerging from a Manhattan manhole went viral on social media. The NYPD confirmed to Fox News Digital that the incident occurred on Aug. 18 at 4:19 a.m. on the southeast corner of 32nd Street and Seventh Avenue, which is near Penn Station. No arrests have been made in this case, but police said they are reviewing surveillance video. NYPD detectives told WABC that they believe many of the people who have been caught on camera doing this are migrants searching for valuables in the sewers. WOMAN DIES AFTER PLUNGING INTO UNCOVERED MANHOLE OUTSIDE LUXURY STORES Detectives said a scavenger culture exists in nations like Venezuela. City officials have said that sneaking into manholes is both illegal and "extremely dangerous." NYPD INVESTIGATING AFTER SURVEILLANCE VIDEO CAPTURES GROUP ENTERING SEWERS THROUGH MANHOLES "DEP has inspected the sewers at the location, and our infrastructure is safe. DEP works closely with our public safety partners to help ensure the safety and security of critical infrastructure throughout New York City," the city's Department of Environmental Protection said in a statement to Fox News Digital. The statement continued: "Entering the sewer system is both illegal and extremely dangerous. Sewers can contain numerous hazards, including noxious and potentially deadly gases, unstable surfaces, flooding risks, and confined spaces. For these reasons, members of the public should never enter a pipe, drain, catch basin, manhole, or outfall." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP New York City's sewer system is made up of an elaborate network of more than 7,400 miles of wastewater and stormwater pipes, parts of which date back to the 1800s. In June, The Associated Press reported on three separate instances of people exiting manholes in Queens and the Williamsburg and Gravesend neighborhoods of Brooklyn. Many of them were wearing headlamps and were carrying shovels or other tools when they were caught on video. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Emilio Azcárraga Milmo, empresario: “México es un país de una clase modesta muy jodida, que no va a salir de jodida. Para la televisión es una obligación llevar diversión a esa gente”
articles.standfirst: El “Tigre” Azcárraga protagonizó una polémica por sus declaraciones sobre la clase modesta de México y el papel de Televisa
articles.summary: El “Tigre” Azcárraga protagonizó una polémica por sus declaraciones sobre la clase modesta de México y el papel de Televisa
articles.body: La televisión mexicana tuvo en Emilio Azcárraga Milmo, conocido como “El Tigre”, a uno de sus personajes más poderosos. Durante los años en que estuvo al frente de Televisa, la empresa no sólo amplió su presencia en México, sino que convirtió sus contenidos en productos de gran alcance internacional. Pero una declaración realizada en 1993 marcó especialmente su trayectoria. En una entrevista con el periodista Alejandro Salazar Hernández, el empresario habló sobre el público de la televisora y utilizó una expresión que décadas después continúa generando controversia: describió a una parte de los mexicanos como una clase “muy jodida” y señaló que la televisión tenía la obligación de entretenerla. La frase apareció durante una conversación publicada en El Nacional, en febrero de 1993. Azcárraga Milmo hablaba sobre el mercado de Televisa y defendía el papel de la empresa como una fuente de entretenimiento para amplios sectores de la población. El empresario también explicó que el mercado de Televisa era principalmente la clase media popular, mientras que los sectores de mayores ingresos tenían otras opciones de entretenimiento. La declaración generó críticas por la manera en que Azcárraga describió la situación económica de millones de mexicanos. Al mismo tiempo, sus palabras reflejaban la visión empresarial que tenía sobre la televisión: un medio cuyo principal atractivo era ofrecer entretenimiento a las mayorías. Emilio Azcárraga Milmo nació en 1930 y fue hijo de Emilio Azcárraga Vidaurreta, fundador de los negocios que posteriormente darían forma al conglomerado televisivo. “El Tigre” asumió el liderazgo de Televisa y durante su gestión la compañía alcanzó una enorme influencia en México y otros países. También estuvo relacionado con el crecimiento del Club América, adquirido por la empresa en 1959. Azcárraga Milmo murió en 1997, a los 66 años, dejando a su hijo Emilio Azcárraga Jean al frente del imperio empresarial. Además de declarar que México era un país de “jodidos” y que nunca iba a salir de esa situación, el padre de Emilio Azcárraga Jean también dijo otras frases bastante polémicas, como: La polémica frase de Azcárraga Milmo, por ello, permanece como parte de la historia de la televisión mexicana y del debate sobre la relación entre medios, entretenimiento y desigualdad social. A futuro, el recuerdo de aquellas palabras seguirá ligado a una pregunta vigente: ¿los medios deben limitarse a entretener o también contribuir a transformar la realidad de su audiencia?

articles.title: Globetrotting sailor nabbed in Canada over alleged child sex crimes aboard sailboat: feds
articles.summary: Donald Steven Lang, 62, was arrested in Canada after the FBI warned the alleged child predator could be sailing across the Pacific to evade authorities.
articles.body: An alleged child predator accused of exploiting a child aboard his sailboat was arrested in Canada, after the FBI warned he could be sailing across the Pacific Ocean to evade authorities. Donald Steven Lang, 62, was taken into custody over the weekend at the request of the United States, federal authorities said Tuesday, ending a far-reaching search for the globe-trotting sailor. Lang, a dual U.S. and Canadian citizen, was indicted Aug. 20 in Hawaii on one count of sexual exploitation of children. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN Prosecutors allege he exploited a minor between September and December 2024 aboard his 55-foot sailboat, Ishi. The Department of Justice (DOJ) said Lang was known to sail around the world and frequently harbored in Hawaii. But the FBI’s search for him extended far beyond the islands. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE LAID BLUEPRINT FOR VANISHING BEFORE 20-YEAR ESCAPE: AFFIDAVIT The bureau warned Lang, who was last seen on board Ishi in Hawaii in January 2025, could have been sailing between Hawaii and Fiji or Mexico, headed toward Papua New Guinea, or possibly Indonesia. He had ties or connections in Hawaii, Idaho, Washington state, California, Fiji, the Marquesas Islands, Mexico and Canada, the FBI said. Federal prosecutors allege that Lang attempted to and knowingly used, persuaded, induced, enticed or coerced a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions. The indictment identifies his sailboat as a 55-foot, 1985 Taylor Hatfield oceangoing sailing vessel. Prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the boat, digital devices and storage media, including a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra phone, should Lang be convicted. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' EX-COP FUGITIVE RETURNED AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN TO FACE MURDER, CHILD SEX CHARGES Lang was already wanted in Idaho in a separate child sex abuse case, authorities said. Kootenai County prosecutors charged Lang in April 2025 with three counts of lewd conduct towards a minor under 16 and one count of sexual battery of a minor in connection with allegations that he sexually assaulted a minor between 2003 and 2007. MORE THAN 300 ARRESTED IN SPRAWLING CALIFORNIA CRACKDOWN ON CHILD EXPLOITATION CRIMES "Protecting children from sexual predators is a priority of the highest order," Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva said. "We will continue to pursue this alleged offender and work with our law enforcement partners to return him to the United States to face trial for the crimes he is charged with committing." FBI Criminal Assistant Director Heith Janke said Lang had been accused by multiple victims of sexually abusing minors. FBI ANNOUNCES 305 ARRESTS, 24 MISSING CHILDREN RECOVERED IN CHICAGO DURING OPERATION NEW DAWN "The FBI remains committed to identifying, investigating, and bringing offenders to justice who prey on some of the most vulnerable members of our communities," Janke said. The FBI had offered a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to Lang’s arrest and warned he should be considered an escape risk. ALLEGED IRISH CARTEL BOSS ARRESTED IN COVERT OPERATION ON ORGANIZED CRIME CHARGES AFTER YEARS-LONG MANHUNT Lang’s apprehension came through cooperation between the FBI and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s Pacific Region, authorities said. The RCMP’s Tofinoofino General Duty, Island District GIS, Nanaimo Detachment and Island District ERT assisted in the arrest, while the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs helped secure it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If convicted in the Hawaii case, Lang faces a mandatory minimum of 15 years in prison and up to 30 years behind bars. He could also face a fine of up to $250,000 and supervised release of between five years and life.

articles.title: California school district sued over field trip to mosque where students allegedly donned Muslim garb
articles.summary: Multi-faith parents sued Palo Alto High School claiming students were given hijabs and Qurans during a mosque field trip last year without parental consent.
articles.body: A group of multi-faith parents has filed a joint lawsuit against Palo Alto Unified School District in California and Palo Alto High School's principal Brent Kline over a field trip to a local mosque last year. According to the August 7 lawsuit, as part of the school's Social Justice Pathway curriculum, students took a tour of a mosque hosted by the Muslim Community Association and took part in several religious activities and were allegedly encouraged to don religious garb without parental consent. "During the Fall 2025 mosque visit, students who were minors allegedly were provided with Muslim religious attire and encouraged to wear it while on site," the complaint read. "During that visit, students allegedly were provided with Qurans and taught that Islam, in particular, promotes social justice." TEXAS TEEN TELLS CONGRESS HE RECEIVED DEATH THREATS AFTER REVEALING ISLAMIC BOOTH AT HIGH SCHOOL "The field-trip activities allegedly included observation of a Dhuhr prayer, discussion of the meaning of worship, and engagement with participants in the Noor Hifz Academy, the host institution’s religious youth program in which Islamic students memorize the Quran," the complaint continued. "Female students were provided hijabs to wear and that all students were gifted Qurans to take home for personal use." The lawsuit, which was filed by a group of Jewish, Hindu and Zoroastrian parents, also claimed that students spoke to Zahra Billoo, the executive director of the Bay Area office of the Council on American-Islamic Relations, who has come under controversy for making allegedly antisemitic statements in the past. In a comment to Fox News Digital, David Rosenberg-Wohl, who is representing the parents, said that the issue at hand is a public school like Palo Alto High School specifically promoting Islam in its Social Justice Pathway curriculum.  "In effect, kids are being told that if they are progressive and interested in social justice, Islam is the faith for them. That is not the business of a public school. It's not an issue of religion v. religion. It's an American one. The separation of church and state is a bedrock issue here," Rosenberg-Wohl said. FORT WORTH PRINCIPAL PICK FACES BACKLASH, INVESTIGATION OVER SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS DEFENDING SHARIA LAW The Muslim Community Association stood by its original statement, saying that the organization was "deeply concerned" over the lawsuit. "Treating students' exposure to ordinary Muslim faith and practice as inherently coercive or threatening risks reinforcing the very Islamophobia and misunderstanding that that educational engagement should help overcome," the group told Fox News Digital. Palo Alto Unified Superintendent Jason Glass informed Fox News Digital that he is reviewing the allegations but "will not comment further on pending litigation." Though some parents were upset by the field trip, some students appeared to defend the outing, suggesting that the grievances were exaggerated. Student newspaper "The Paly Voice" editor-in-chief Juni Thurston disputed claims that female students were forced to don hijabs and that students were indoctrinated with Islamic beliefs on these trips. DEARBORN SCHOOLS APOLOGIZE AFTER 200-PLUS STUDENTS MISTAKENLY SERVED PORK DURING RAMADAN "The vast majority of the people demonizing the teachers who arranged and chaperoned this field trip simply don’t know them," Thurston wrote in an op-ed for the campus newspaper. "The idea that they would be working to indoctrinate students into Islam, or any religion, is an idea extremely foreign to me as a student who has had them as my teachers for the past two years. But this narrative is nonetheless dominating media coverage of the event." However, she acknowledged concerns over Billoo's presence on the field trip and agreed that she should not have been part of the experience, though her role was "limited." In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE) Vice President of Strategic Initiatives Adam Goldstein said that if students were compelled to don religious garb, this would be in violation of the First Amendment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Just as the First Amendment prevents public schools from forcing students to pledge allegiance to the flag, it prevents those schools from compelling them to wear religious attire. If students were required to do that as part of a curricular field trip, it would conflict with the First Amendment's bar on compelled speech," Goldstein said.

articles.title: AMLO vuelve a CDMX para defender a Andy López Beltrán, revela Riva Palacio
articles.standfirst: El periodista señala que el expresidente está temeroso de las investigaciones a su hijo
articles.summary: El periodista señala que el expresidente está temeroso de las investigaciones a su hijo
articles.body: Luego de que se diera a conocer que le retiraron la visa a Andrés López Beltrán, el expresidente de México, Andrés Manuel López Obrador salió de su residencia en Palenque para instalarse una vez más en la Ciudad de México ante las investigaciones del gobierno de los Estados Unidos en contra de su hijo, por lo que el periodista Raymundo Riva Palacio, asegura que AMLO está temeroso y por eso regresó a la capital del país. La información la reveló el periodista, una semana después de que se le retirara la visa al hijo de AMLO luego del avance de las investigaciones contra Andrés López Beltrán, por lo que ya planea su defensa e incluso busca sacarlo del país. El periodista Raymundo Riva Palacio señaló que el expresidente de México dejó Palenque luego de que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos le retirara la visa a su hijo, Andrés López Beltrán y además, señala que está temeroso de las invetigaciones en su contra y ya planea una estrategia para defenderlo. Incluso, señala Riva Palacio, entre lo que contempla AMLO, es sacar del país a Andrés López Beltrán, "enviándolo a un país 'fuera del alcance' del gobierno de los Estados Unidos, aunque es poco probable pues gente cercana al expresidente le recomendaron que sacarlo de México, es admitir que tiene culpabilidad de lo que es investigado. Además, se supo también que entre los países que tenía contemplado enviar a Andrés López Beltrán era China y Rusia, sin embargo, en estos países tendrían contemplano no aceptar la petición para no abrir un nuevo confilcto con el gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esas no fueron las únicas opciones, también se contempló Sudáfrica pero el periodista reveló que también fue rechazada: "El país que finalmente pensaron fue Sudáfrica y establecieron contacto con funcionarios de esa nación para sondear la posibilidad que ni siquiera llegó a formalizarse por el rechazo que tuvieron de origen". Varias investigaciones apuntan que André López Beltrán tiene nexos con el huachicol fiscal, además de estar vinculado altráfico de influencias, a todo esto, agrega el periodista que la situación escaló luego de que según investigaciones, el general Gerardo Mérida entregara "información sobre la presunta relación de Andrés López Beltrán con los Chapitos y con quienes Rocha Moya había pactado la traición al jefe del Cártel de Sinaloa, Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada".

articles.title: Attempted drone incursion at Virginia prison leads to $324K contraband haul with meth, 17 cellphones
articles.summary: A drone smuggling attempt at a Virginia prison led to a $324,000 contraband seizure including methamphetamine and 17 cellphones, officials said.
articles.body: Virginia prison officials intercepted a package containing an estimated $324,000 worth of contraband, including a pound of suspected methamphetamine and more than a dozen cellphones, following an attempted drone incursion at a state prison, authorities said. The Virginia Department of Corrections (VADOC) said corrections staff discovered the "suspicious package" at Sussex I State Prison at around 1:30 a.m. Monday. Inside, officials said they found a one-pound bag of suspected methamphetamine, 17 cellphones with charging cables and 20 sheets of paper that appeared to be saturated with an unknown liquid. FEDERAL INMATES MAY SOON GET TABLETS WITH MESSAGING CAPABILITIES AS BUREAU OF PRISONS MAKES MODERNIZATION PUSH The agency said it also seized multiple hex wrenches, three USB Wi-Fi adapters and two SIM cards. Officials also discovered an unusual assortment of other items, including 30 disposable lighters, two cartons of cigarettes, one pound of loose-leaf tobacco, three packs of cigars, two bottles of professional-grade tattoo ink, two bottles of perfume and two bottles of glue. WILD VIDEO SHOWS INMATES RIOTING INSIDE JAIL AFTER FRUSTRATIONS OVER ACCESS BOIL OVER VADOC estimated the contraband had a combined value of roughly $324,000 inside the prison. VADOC Director Joseph Walters said the seizure highlighted the sophisticated methods people may use in attempts to smuggle contraband into correctional facilities. DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS "This investigation is an important reminder that some people will use sophisticated methods in an attempt to smuggle drugs and other dangerous contraband into Virginia Department of Corrections facilities," Walters said in a statement. "I thank our institutional staff at Sussex I State Prison for their vigilance and focus on ensuring the safety and security of our facility," he continued. "Our dedicated correctional staff and OLES members stand ready to intercept any dangerous contraband that individuals may attempt to introduce into correctional settings to ensure the safety and security of our dedicated corrections team members, of incarcerated individuals in our custody, of probationers, and of people in communities all across the Commonwealth of Virginia." The incident remains under investigation by VADOC's Office of Law Enforcement Services (OLES).
